start.description: start date for the data point

outlierCode.description:
outlierCode: 0 or no value -- regular point
             1 -- to be ignored when returning results of value outlier analysis
             2 -- is an estimated value
             3 -- combination of 1 and 2 together

enum (0, 1, 2)

comments.description: (Optional) any comments for the data point

isEstimated.description: Denotes if the value is an actual value or an estimated value. default = null (actual value)

dataVersion.description:
Same data points can have different data version to denote priority. Default behavior in case of overlapping
data points is to pick the data point with the highest data version.
If data version is not specified, then default (avg) overlap handling is applied to the overalapping data points

statusCode.description: Customer specific status code for the data point (may be used to denote data quality)

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

contribution.description:
The contribution value associated with the model prediction or reliability assessment.
This value could represent the importance, significance, or impact of a given prediction in the context
of the overall model output or reliability model.
`@ts(treatmentPath='parent.treatment')` - Specifies the path to retrieve the treatment value from the parent entity.
The treatment may involve scaling, adjusting, or interpreting the value based on specific treatment rules or configurations.

contributionUpperBound.description:
The upper bound for the contribution value.
This defines the maximum permissible value for the contribution. This can be useful for ensuring that
the model predictions or assessments do not exceed a certain threshold, whether for business logic or for safety concerns.
For example, if the contribution represents the percentage impact of a model, the upper bound may be constrained to 100%.

contributionLowerBound.description:
The lower bound for the contribution value.
This defines the minimum permissible value for the contribution. It ensures that the contribution does not
fall below a predefined threshold, which may be useful for avoiding overly small or negative values that are not meaningful in the given context.
For example, in reliability models, a negative contribution may be illogical, so the lower bound might ensure that the value is positive.

title:
Represents a contribution related to model predictions, such as machine learning model outputs
or reliability assessments. This entity captures a contribution value with associated upper and lower bounds,
which may be used in various predictive or diagnostic applications for tracking model contributions and assessing their significance.
This entity type mixes the properties of `TimedDataPoint` and includes metadata from `ReliabilityMl.ContributionHeader`.
The fields provided here allow storing and tracking the contribution value over time, along with its bounds for validation purposes.
For details on other information stored in this Type, refer to the documentation on each of the fields of this Type.
name: ReliabilityMl.Contribution
